title: ParsiPrakashVinodVedangRai563GhaAlm3Shlf4DevanagariJyotish
shelf_note: A Devanagari paper manuscript of a Persian-for-Sanskrit-readers grammar/lexicon (Persian verb forms in Devanagari, each with its Sanskrit equivalent), in the eGangotri / Dharmartha Trust J&K collection. That matches the collections listed. '1643' is presumably the date of the work, not of this copy.
structure_note: The counts disagree with each other: 110 page records, all with OCR, against pages_count 42; pages_translated 0 in the structure counts against pages_translated_field 42, yet this page carries a translation (E2-type instrument mismatch). Only 19 pages have a printed number, and this leaf has two in its margin (Devanagari २४ with a later Western 14). The 4 backsteps and 3 repeats are most likely the parser switching between these two numberings, or misreading Devanagari numerals, rather than leaves out of order. That is not confirmed from one page.

pages.printed_marker: २४ (with a later hand's "14" beneath, left margin)
pages.layout: single-column oblong pothi-style leaf, 11 lines of Devanagari, folio numbers in the left margin, repository stamp line at the foot

tr_errors.problem: Nothing on the page says 'they': the OCR has bhavaty-arthe ('he becomes'), and the image shows 'bhavāmīty-arthe meśavaṃ' ('I become'). The person is wrong in a conjugation paradigm.

tr_errors.english: In the sense of "may I become," **Tu-śave** is stated.
tr_errors.problem: bhavāmi is indicative ('I become'), not optative

missing.why: Nothing explains what this form is (in the image it is probably a subjunctive 'bi-khuram', 'that I may eat'). As it stands, a reader cannot make sense of 'in the sense of "I"'.

book_verdict: The right leaf, with a careful translation that names its uncertainty and has mostly sound Persian-identification notes. But the cursive Devanagari OCR has several meaning-bearing misreads (शु→शृ, हनने→रूनने, पुक्त→मुक्त) that the English headwords carry, and the opening note and sentence assign the wrong person ('they become'). Book counts are internally inconsistent (110 records vs 42; 0 vs 42 translated). The CC-0 eGangotri stamp at the foot is a public-domain mark, not a rights problem.
